purpose: Define the exact exit-code value each of six caliper-docgen CLI subcommands (extract, watch, check, inspect, schema, completions) returns for every reachable termination path (clean run, diagnostic-driven exit_code(), argument-parse rejection, and Err-propagation-to-main), the structural rule that process::exit is called from exactly one normal-path site, and schema output field-completeness, so CI and pre-commit pipelines can script against exit codes without guessing at undocumented process::exit behavior. lsp's exit codes are covered entirely by SPEC-CLI-001c, since lsp is a long-running server rather than a run-to-completion command.
scope: The exit-code-producing paths of crates/cli/src/main.rs and crates/cli/src/commands/{extract,watch,check,inspect,schema,completions}.rs (lsp.rs excluded, see SPEC-CLI-001c): which exit code each command returns for a clean run, an Error-severity diagnostic, a Warning-severity diagnostic under --strict, an argument clap itself rejects during parsing (exit 2, AC-015/AC-020), an argument value clap accepts but a command handler rejects (exit 1, AC-021), and an Err returned from a command handler (including a config-load failure). Also covers schema's JSON-Schema output field-completeness (AC-016). Does not cover file-write atomicity (SPEC-CLI-001b) or config-loading semantics/precedence/error-message content (SPEC-CLI-001d) beyond the exit code a config failure produces.
non_goals: The extraction/resolution logic itself (parsing TSX, resolving prop types, building ComponentEntry) — owned by crates/core, a separate capability under a separate spec.
NAPI/Node binding entry points — owned by crates/binding, a separate capability.
Adding a --strict flag to extract, watch, or inspect. Only check exposes --strict today; this asymmetry is documented as intentional-for-now and out of scope for this revision.
File write atomicity and error-surfacing mechanics for extract --out / watch --out — covered by SPEC-CLI-001b.
LSP Content-Length parsing, buffer allocation, framing, and the lsp subcommand's exit codes — covered entirely by SPEC-CLI-001c.

Config loading, evaluation-failure messages, and precedence rules — covered by SPEC-CLI-001d; this spec asserts only that a config-load failure in extract/watch/check/inspect produces exit code 1 (AC-018), not what the error message contains.

Replacing watch's keyboard-quit thread's std::process::exit call with a graceful watchexec action.quit()/signals() handshake so watchexec's own main-loop return path is reached on keyboard quit instead of bypassed. The hard-exit already carries the correct tracked exit code (AC-007/AC-008) — routing it through watchexec's graceful shutdown instead is a code-quality follow-up, not a correctness gap this spec requires closing.

Confirming that pressing 'q'/'c' actually invokes std::process::exit with the tracked value end-to-end. AC-007/AC-008 assert only the tracked exit-code value itself (verifiable via the existing unit tests on watch_exit_code, and via the AtomicI32 store inside the Watchexec::new action closure that runs after each file-change event), not the keypress-to-process-exit wiring — that wiring is grounded directly in source (the keyboard thread's KeyCode match arm) but confirming it via an automated keypress requires a PTY harness this codebase doesn't have. Building that harness is separate infrastructure work.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Running extract against a source directory that produces zero Error-severity diagnostics returns exit code 0.
Running extract against a source directory that produces at least one Error-severity diagnostic (e.g. a nonexistent --src path) returns exit code 2, identically whether or not --json is passed.
Running check against a source directory that produces zero diagnostics of Warning or Error severity returns exit code 0.

Running check against a source directory that produces at least one Error-severity diagnostic returns exit code 2, whether or not --json is passed and whether or not --strict is passed — Error-severity always takes precedence over the --strict/Warning-only path in AC-005, even when both an Error and a Warning are present in the same diagnostic set.
Running check --strict against a source directory that produces at least one Warning-severity diagnostic and zero Error-severity diagnostics returns exit code 1.
Running check (without --strict) against the same Warning-only source directory as AC-005 returns exit code 0.

After a file-change event in a watch session whose cumulative diagnostic snapshot (session.snapshot(), not just that event's own delta) contains at least one Error-severity diagnostic, watch's tracked exit-code value — the value both cmd_watch's own graceful-loop-exit return statement and the keyboard-quit thread's KeyCode::Char('q') | KeyCode::Char('c') arm read — is 2. This also holds for the initial startup snapshot before any file-change event, if that snapshot itself contains an Error-severity diagnostic.

After a file-change event in a watch session whose cumulative diagnostic snapshot contains no Error-severity diagnostic (including the initial startup snapshot, before any file-change event has occurred), watch's tracked exit-code value is 0.

Sending SIGINT to a running watch process does not terminate it. watchexec 8.2.0 installs its own SIGINT handler that replaces the OS's default disposition and forwards the interrupt as an Event to the action closure instead of terminating the process directly; since the closure in watch.rs never calls action.signals() or action.quit(), that event is dropped and the watch session continues running unaffected — file-change extraction, and (when --out PATH is set) snapshot writes to PATH, continue after SIGINT is sent.

If watchexec's own event loop terminates with a CriticalError (e.g. the underlying filesystem-watching backend fails during setup or operation), or if config loading fails for the --config/docgen.config.ts path (per SPEC-CLI-001d), cmd_watch returns Err rather than any exit_code-derived value. This Err propagates out of main() via the ? on cmd_watch's call site, causing main() to print the error to stderr and exit with code 1 — distinct from AC-007/AC-008/AC-009.
Running inspect COMPONENT where COMPONENT is present as a key in ExtractionOutput.components and no file in the scanned source tree has an Error-severity diagnostic returns exit code 0.

Running inspect COMPONENT where COMPONENT is present as a key in ExtractionOutput.components but a different file elsewhere in the scanned source tree has an Error-severity diagnostic (e.g. a parse error) returns exit code 2, not 0.

Running inspect COMPONENT where COMPONENT is not among the extracted components' names returns exit code 1, with an error printed to stderr that names the requested component and lists the available component names.

Running completions with a shell value clap_complete::Shell recognizes (bash, zsh, fish, powershell, or elvish) writes the generated completion script to stdout and exits code 0, independent of any source directory or extraction state — cmd_completions never calls pipeline::extract.

Running completions with a shell argument that does not match any of clap_complete::Shell's recognized values is rejected by clap during argument parsing itself, before any command handler runs. The process prints a usage error to stderr and exits with code 2 — a different failure mechanism from extract/check's diagnostic-driven exit code 2, despite sharing the same numeric value.

Serializing an ExtractionOutput built from exactly: one ComponentEntry whose props map is non-empty, whose inheritance list is non-empty, and whose tags list is non-empty; one Diagnostic whose file, line, column, and help fields are all Some(_); and an ExtractionStats whose every numeric field is non-zero — to JSON produces no field name that is absent from the schema command's printed JSON Schema output.

main() is the only site in the crate that calls std::process::exit for a command's own success/failure signaling on the normal (non-Err) path: cmd_extract, cmd_watch, cmd_check, and cmd_inspect each return their exit code as an i32 (or Result<i32>) value from an ordinary function call, assertable directly in a unit test without spawning a subprocess. The sole exception is watch's detached keyboard-input thread, which calls std::process::exit directly with the tracked value described in AC-007/AC-008, since it has no return path back to main(). Any command handler returning Err (config-load failure, missing component, watchexec CriticalError) terminates the process via main()'s own ?-propagation and Rust's Result Termination at exit code 1, not via a direct std::process::exit call anywhere in command-handler code.

Running extract, check, or inspect with a --config path that fails to load (per SPEC-CLI-001d's failure conditions) returns Err from the command handler rather than any exit_code()-derived value; this Err propagates out of main() via ?, printing the error to stderr and exiting with code 1 — the same mechanism AC-010 asserts for watch.
Running schema writes the JSON Schema to stdout and exits code 0, independent of any source directory, --config value, or extraction state — cmd_schema never calls pipeline::extract or build_options.

Invoking any of extract, watch, check, inspect, schema, or completions with a missing required argument (e.g. inspect with no COMPONENT positional), an unrecognized flag, or a value clap rejects for a value_enum argument (e.g. extract --format bogus, extract --html-attributes bogus) is rejected by clap during argument parsing before any command handler runs; the process prints a usage error to stderr and exits with code 2, by the same clap-level mechanism as AC-015.

Running extract with a --react-version value that is neither "react18" nor "react19" is accepted by clap (the flag is typed as a plain Option<String> on ExtractArgs, not a value_enum, and is not global) but rejected by build_options, which returns Err; that Err propagates out of main() via ?, printing the error to stderr and exiting with code 1 — not the exit code 2 of the clap-level rejection path in AC-020. (--react-version is declared only on ExtractArgs; passing it to watch, check, or inspect is itself an unrecognized-flag rejection under AC-020, exit code 2, not AC-021's exit 1.)
